A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same VAPT research despite changes in title and presentation. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A-E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original classification experiments, sample-efficiency measurements, ablations, and visualization results in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v5 retains those original results and adds ADE20K segmentation results and statistical analyses in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The channel-wise convolution, token-wise projectors, shared feature projector, ReLU activation, LayerNorm, and adaptive-prompt equations remain unchanged. Applying VAPT to segmentation does not introduce a documented change to its procedure.

E1.justification: v5 adds ADE20K semantic segmentation, extending evaluation from image classification to dense prediction (Section 6.1 and Appendix E.5). The original 24 FGVC and VTAB-1K classification tasks remain covered.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained classification experiments is unchanged. The new segmentation comparison applies existing full-tuning, head-only, bias-tuning, and VPT strategies. The adaptive prompting methods newly discussed in Appendix C are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The added ADE20K experiment introduces evaluation with a ViT-L-based segmentation model and mIoU (Table 16). Existing classification splits, preprocessing, training schedules, backbone comparisons, and sample-efficiency procedures are retained.

E4.justification: The component, convolution, and linear-activation ablations are retained as Tables 17-19, formerly Tables 15-17. Backbone scaling, hyperparameter sensitivity, sample-efficiency experiments, and GradCAM case studies also retain their evidence despite relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: v5 adds one-tailed paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across 19 VTAB tasks against five baselines, specifying hypotheses and a 0.05 significance threshold (Appendix E.3, Table 15). Three-run averaging and standard-deviation reporting already appeared in v4 and remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All retained tables match numerically. New Table 16 reports ADE20K mIoU of 44.04 for VAPT, 42.24 for VPT, 43.40 for Bias, 35.12 for Head, and 48.31 for Full. Table 15 adds five p-values below 0.05. These are additional results, not improvements over v4 under retained settings.

T1.justification: The MoE formulation, Voronoi losses, assumptions, Proposition 1, Theorems 1-2, and proofs in Appendices A-B remain substantively unchanged. Proof edits improve wording without revising the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central expressiveness, sample-efficiency, parameter-efficiency, and classification-performance claims remain. v5 modestly broadens the conclusion by explicitly suggesting that the MoE-based analysis extends to other Transformer variants; v4 discussed architectural extensions only as future work.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly distinguishes static prompt experts from their input-dependent gating functions and adds explanations about preserving pretrained experts relative to alternative adaptive prompting approaches. It also interprets segmentation results as evidence of broader applicability and removes v4's classification-only limitation.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly identifies SETR-PUP as the framework for the segmentation experiment, complemented by the ViT-L specification in Table 16. Appendix D retains the classification recipes, PyTorch implementation, A100-40GB hardware, and promised future code release. Detailed segmentation training instructions are not added.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds substantive positioning against existing adaptive prompting research, including diversity-aware meta visual prompting, continual-learning adaptive prompts, Pro-tuning, SA2VP, and CVPT. It distinguishes layer-specific conditioning, preservation of pretrained experts, and theoretical tractability, addressing close prior approaches absent from v4's discussion.

P1.justification: v5 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, motivation, method explanations, and proof prose. It changes the title and author-affiliation block, moves references before the supplement, and reorganizes the experimental appendix around the added analyses.

P2.justification: v5 substantially changes typography, spacing, display sizing, and placement. It removes v4's VPT propagation and convolution schematics, adds Tables 15-16, integrates previously separate appendix displays with nearby text, and wraps text around the retained sample-efficiency figure and table.

improvement.justification: Compared with v4's classification-only evaluation, ADE20K results provide evidence of broader applicability. The Wilcoxon tests strengthen comparative support, and Appendix C better explains novelty relative to prior adaptive prompting. The core method, theory, and original results remain stable; sparse segmentation training details and removal of two explanatory schematics limit the overall gain.
